title: Sandglass-Typed Single Chameleon Luminophore for Water Mapping Measurements: Intramolecular Energy Migrations in the Hydrophilic Tb(III)/Sm(III) Cluster

synthesis.procedure: Sal-TEG-2 (314.0 mg, 0.957 mmol) was dissolved in methanol (10 mL) and triethylamine (192.0 mg, 1.89 mmol) was added with stirring at 40 °C. Tb(NO3)3·6H2O (265.0 mg; reported as 585.0 mmol, chemically corresponding to 0.585 mmol) in methanol (10 mL) was added dropwise and the mixture was stirred for 30 min, giving a white powder. Recrystallization from methanol/water afforded a white powder; single crystals used for X-ray analysis were obtained by recrystallization from ethanol.

properties.summary: Water- and methanol-soluble green Tb(III) emitter. Φ ≈ 38–40% and τ ≈ 1.1–1.2 ms at 295 K; solid-state τ = 0.98 ms at 100 K. Relative thermal sensitivity Sr of the 547 nm band in water (273–310 K) is 0.48% K−1. Arrhenius analysis of emission lifetime gave a BEnT activation energy of 1960 cm−1.

properties.summary: Single-molecule chameleon thermometer in water: green luminescence at 20 °C and yellow at 50 °C under 375 nm excitation. The I_Tb(547 nm)/I_Sm ratio varies linearly with temperature. Sr of the 547 nm Tb band in water is 0.94% K−1 (273–310 K), larger than Tb9-Sal-PEG-4. Solid-state τ = 0.83 ms at 100 K. Color change requires intramolecular Tb–Sm energy transfer in one mixed cluster rather than a physical mixture of homometallic clusters.
